title: Enumeration and Successor of Valid Records
statement: For every natural number $k$ and finite decidable types $Q,T$, there is a family of finite lists $E_{n,s}$ of records, with no repetitions, such that a record belongs to $E_{n,s}$ exactly when it encodes a configuration on a binary input of length $n$, together with a tag, whose work-tape heads and nonblank cells lie within distance $s$ of the origin. There are also a natural number $K$, a finite decidable state type $P$, a deterministic machine $R$ with $K+2$ work tapes over the record alphabet, distinct decision states $\mathrm{yes},\mathrm{no}$, designated states $\mathrm{first},\mathrm{next}$, and a constant $C$ that perform the following bounded transitions. On a configuration in state $\mathrm{first}$ with the prescribed blank first tape, the machine writes the first record of $E_{n,s}$ on that tape and enters $\mathrm{yes}$, or enters $\mathrm{no}$ if the list is empty. On a configuration in state $\mathrm{next}$ whose first tape encodes its $i$th record, it writes the next record and enters $\mathrm{yes}$, or enters $\mathrm{no}$ when there is no next record. In both cases it preserves all other configuration data, avoids both decision states before the final time, and keeps every head within distance $C(L+|\langle H\rangle|+1)$ of its initial position through that time, where $L$ is the prescribed record length and $H$ is the fixed template record; the time is at most $C^{L+|\langle H\rangle|+1}$. The input record is encoded on work tape $1$ according to the template, and all tapes of index at least $2$ are blank.
hypotheses_covered: For the first-record transition: state $\mathrm{first}$ and blank first tape over the prescribed interval
For the successor transition: index $i$ is within the enumeration, state $\mathrm{next}$, and tape $0$ stores the $i$th record
All work tapes of index at least $2$ are blank
